headline: Google has agreed with Constellation Energy to buy about 3.6 gigawatts of nuclear-backed power on the largest US grid for its data centers.
score_reason: Pool 9 kept: confirmed by both companies, large (about 3.6 GW, over $4.3 billion of investment) and it confirms yesterday's Bloomberg report.
importance_line: It shows AI companies paying to expand existing nuclear plants and reserve existing output, which affects power customers on the PJM grid (about 67 million people), utilities and rival data center builders, though the extra supply arrives only from 2028 and the price of the power was not disclosed.
source: Quartz, relaying a Google and Constellation Energy announcement
summary: Quartz reports that Google and Constellation Energy, the largest US nuclear plant operator, announced on 6 Oct 2026 a 20-year agreement under which Google buys 890 megawatts of new nuclear capacity on the PJM grid (the largest US power market), made by upgrading 11 Constellation reactors in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey with more than $4.3 billion of investment, the first upgrade due by 2028. The companies also signed a separate 15-year supply deal for another 2,700 megawatts from Constellation's existing plants, about 3.6 gigawatts in all, which confirms the deal Bloomberg reported as near in our 6 Oct edition.
